paper.title: Prospective association between ultra-processed food consumption and incident depressive symptoms in the French NutriNet-Santé cohort
paper.authors: Adjibade M, Julia C, Allès B, Touvier M, Lemogne C, Srour B, Hercberg S, Galan P, Assmann KE, Kesse-Guyot E.

study.population: Adults aged 18–86 years from the NutriNet-Santé cohort in France, followed prospectively

exposure.name: UPF proportion
exposure.definition: Proportion of ultra-processed foods (%UPF) in the diet, calculated from 24-h dietary records and classified using the NOVA system

outcome.name: Incident depressive symptoms
outcome.definition: New onset of depressive symptoms identified by CES-D score ≥ 17 in men and ≥ 23 in women at any follow-up assessment

missing_confounders.label: Sleep deprivation
missing_confounders.rationale: Poor sleep increases the risk of developing depressive symptoms and may lead individuals to choose convenient, ultra‑processed foods due to fatigue and altered appetite regulation.

evidence.title: Sleep deprivation makes us less happy, more anxious
Effect of Inadequate Sleep on Frequent Mental Distress
How sleep deprivation can harm your health - Harvard Health

missing_confounders.review_note: Sleep deprivation may be a consequence of high UPF intake (diet affects sleep quality) and thus adjusting for it could block a mediating pathway rather than control confounding.

missing_confounders.label: Social isolation
missing_confounders.rationale: Loneliness and lack of social support are strong predictors of depression and can increase reliance on ready‑to‑eat ultra‑processed meals when cooking for others is less frequent.

evidence.title: Ultra-Processed Food Is Positively Associated With Depressive ...
Relationship between 39 dietary markers of ultra-processed food ...
CE corner: The risks of social isolation

missing_confounders.review_note: Social isolation predicts both greater reliance on ultra‑processed foods and incident depressive symptoms and is not captured by the adjusted covariates (marital status alone does not measure broader loneliness).

missing_confounders.label: Chronic illness
missing_confounders.rationale: Conditions such as cardiovascular disease or diabetes raise depression risk and often necessitate diets higher in processed foods due to physical limitations or dietary recommendations.

evidence.title: The risk associated with ultra-processed food intake on depressive symptoms and mental health in older adults: a target trial emulation | BMC Medicine | Springer Nature Link
The Science of Ultra-Processed Foods and Mental Health
Ultra-processed foods: increased risk of depression and anxiety

missing_confounders.review_note: Chronic illnesses such as cardiovascular disease or diabetes are likely downstream effects of high UPF consumption, so adjusting for them would introduce bias by controlling for a mediator.

missing_confounders.label: Family depression
missing_confounders.rationale: A family history of depression reflects genetic and shared environmental susceptibility to depression and may correlate with familial dietary patterns that include higher ultra‑processed food intake.

evidence.title: The risk associated with ultra-processed food intake on depressive symptoms and mental health in older adults: a target trial emulation | BMC Medicine | Springer Nature Link
Frontiers | Ultra-Processed Food Is Positively Associated With Depressive Symptoms Among United States Adults
The Science of Ultra-Processed Foods and Mental Health

missing_confounders.review_note: Family history of depression is a pre‑existing common cause of both depressive symptoms and familial dietary patterns (including UPF) and is not already adjusted for.

missing_confounders.label: Neuroticism
missing_confounders.rationale: High neuroticism predisposes individuals to depressive symptoms and is associated with emotional eating of ultra‑processed foods as a coping mechanism.

evidence.title: Frontiers | Ultra-Processed Food Is Positively Associated With Depressive Symptoms Among United States Adults
The Science of Ultra-Processed Foods and Mental Health
Association Between Ultra-Processed Food Consumption and Risk of Developing Depression in Adults: A Systematic Review - European Medical Journal

missing_confounders.review_note: Neuroticism is a stable personality trait that elevates depression risk and promotes emotional eating of ultra‑processed foods, satisfying confounder criteria and absent from the adjustment set.
